outputs.L1: A sensor failure diagnostic apparatus includes: a first estimation unit configured to estimate a mixing ratio of each type of molecular structure included in a fuel, based on combustion parameters sensed by a combustion sensor when combustion in an internal combustion engine is performed under different combustion conditions; a second estimation unit configured to estimate the mixing ratio based on characteristic parameters sensed by a characteristic sensor; a combustion sensor diagnostic unit configured to determine whether the combustion sensor has failed, based on a sensed value of the combustion sensor when combustion is not being performed; and a characteristic sensor diagnostic unit configured to determine whether the characteristic sensor has failed by comparing the mixing ratio estimated by the first estimation unit with the mixing ratio estimated by the second estimation unit when the combustion sensor diagnostic unit determines that the combustion sensor is normal.
outputs.L2: A sensor fault diagnosis device is provided with several functional units. A first estimation unit calculates the proportion of each molecular-structure type contained in a fuel, using combustion parameters detected by a combustion sensor while combustion in an internal combustion engine is carried out under multiple combustion conditions. A second estimation unit determines the same proportions using characteristic parameters measured by a characteristic sensor. A combustion sensor diagnostic unit judges whether the combustion sensor has failed, based on the value detected by the combustion sensor when combustion is not being performed. A characteristic sensor diagnostic unit determines whether the characteristic sensor is faulty by comparing the mixing ratio calculated by the first estimation unit with the mixing ratio calculated by the second estimation unit, but only when the combustion sensor diagnostic unit has judged that the combustion sensor is operating normally.
outputs.L3:
The apparatus is configured to diagnose sensor failures in a system that performs fuel combustion in an internal combustion engine. In this system, accurate sensor operation is important because information obtained from the sensors is used to evaluate the properties of the fuel and to control combustion appropriately.

The apparatus includes a first estimation unit that estimates a mixing ratio of different molecular structure types contained in the fuel. This estimation is performed on the basis of combustion parameters detected during operation of the engine. The combustion parameters are sensed under different combustion conditions, allowing the first estimation unit to infer the molecular structure composition of the fuel from changes in combustion behavior.

The apparatus also includes a second estimation unit that estimates the same mixing ratio of molecular structure types in the fuel. Unlike the first estimation unit, the second estimation unit performs this estimation using characteristic parameters detected by a characteristic sensor. These characteristic parameters represent properties of the fuel that are related to its molecular structure, and therefore can be used as another basis for estimating the fuel composition.

A combustion sensor diagnostic unit is provided to determine whether the combustion sensor has failed. This diagnostic unit evaluates the sensed value of the combustion sensor when combustion is not being executed. Since the combustion sensor should indicate a known or expected condition during a non-combustion state, an abnormal sensed value in this state can be used to determine that the combustion sensor is malfunctioning.

The apparatus further includes a characteristic sensor diagnostic unit that diagnoses failure of the characteristic sensor. This diagnosis is carried out by comparing the mixing ratio estimated by the first estimation unit with the mixing ratio estimated by the second estimation unit. However, this comparison is performed when the combustion sensor diagnostic unit has determined that the combustion sensor is normal. By first confirming that the combustion sensor is operating properly, the apparatus can use the mixing ratio estimated from combustion parameters as a reliable reference for evaluating the output of the characteristic sensor. If the two estimated mixing ratios differ beyond an allowable range, the characteristic sensor diagnostic unit determines that the characteristic sensor may have failed.
outputs.L4:
A sensor failure diagnostic apparatus is provided for diagnosing abnormalities in sensors used to determine fuel properties in an internal combustion engine. The apparatus estimates a molecular-structure mixing ratio of fuel, such as a mixing ratio relating to hydrocarbon structure or fuel composition, based on combustion parameters obtained under a plurality of different engine combustion conditions. These combustion parameters may include values reflecting ignition timing, combustion timing, heat release, knocking tendency, exhaust characteristics, or other information that changes according to the combustion behavior of the fuel.

The apparatus also separately estimates the molecular-structure mixing ratio of the fuel using characteristic parameters detected by one or more fuel characteristic sensors. Such characteristic parameters may include, for example, density, viscosity, refractive index, dielectric constant, distillation-related information, or other sensor outputs that represent physical or chemical characteristics of the fuel. By obtaining two independently derived estimates of the fuel molecular-structure mixing ratio, the apparatus can evaluate whether the relevant sensors are operating correctly.

In operation, the apparatus first determines whether a combustion sensor has failed by using values obtained from sensors other than the combustion sensor. If the diagnostic result indicates that the combustion sensor is abnormal, the apparatus can identify a failure of the combustion sensor without relying on its own output. If the combustion sensor is determined to be normal, the apparatus then compares the molecular-structure mixing ratio estimated from the combustion parameters with the molecular-structure mixing ratio estimated from the characteristic sensor parameters. When the difference between these two estimated values exceeds a predetermined allowable range, the apparatus determines that a characteristic sensor failure has occurred.

Through this diagnostic sequence, the apparatus avoids misidentifying a characteristic sensor as faulty when the combustion sensor itself is abnormal. Conversely, when the combustion sensor is confirmed to be normal, the comparison between the two independently estimated fuel composition values enables accurate detection of abnormalities in the characteristic sensor. As a result, the reliability of fuel sensing diagnostics is improved, and the engine control system can more accurately respond to changes in fuel composition while preventing erroneous sensor failure determinations.
outputs.L5:
**A Sensor Failure**

A sensor failure occurs when a sensor stops working correctly or provides inaccurate data. Sensors are used in many systems, such as cars, factories, medical devices, security systems, and smart home equipment. When one fails, the system may receive wrong information, react incorrectly, or stop functioning altogether.

There are several possible causes of a sensor failure. The sensor may be damaged by heat, moisture, dust, vibration, or physical impact. Electrical problems, poor wiring, software errors, or lack of maintenance can also lead to failure. In some cases, the sensor may still operate but send inaccurate readings, which can be more dangerous than a complete shutdown because the problem may not be noticed immediately.

The effects of a sensor failure depend on the system involved. In a vehicle, a failed sensor could affect braking, engine performance, or safety systems. In an industrial machine, it could cause production errors or equipment damage. In healthcare, incorrect sensor readings could lead to wrong decisions about a patient’s condition.

To prevent sensor failure, regular inspection, calibration, and maintenance are important. Systems should also be designed with warning signals or backup sensors to detect faults quickly. By identifying and fixing sensor problems early, it is possible to improve safety, reliability, and performance.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for a sensor failure diagnostic apparatus for an internal combustion engine that estimates fuel molecular structure mixing ratios using both combustion parameters and characteristic sensor data.
counterfactuals.output: A sensor failure diagnostic apparatus for an internal combustion engine includes a combustion-state acquisition unit configured to acquire combustion parameters indicative of an in-cylinder combustion condition, a sensor-data acquisition unit configured to acquire characteristic sensor data corresponding to a property of fuel supplied to the engine, and an estimation unit configured to estimate a molecular-structure mixing ratio of the fuel based on both the combustion parameters and the characteristic sensor data. The apparatus further includes a comparison unit configured to compare a first mixing ratio estimated from the combustion parameters with a second mixing ratio estimated from the characteristic sensor data, and a diagnostic unit configured to determine a failure state of at least one sensor when a deviation between the first and second mixing ratios exceeds a predetermined threshold or exhibits a predetermined abnormal pattern. The apparatus thereby distinguishes sensor abnormality from fuel-quality variation and enables accurate diagnosis of sensor failure during engine operation.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an invention for diagnosing failures of fuel-related sensors in an internal combustion engine, where one estimator uses combustion data under different conditions and another uses characteristic sensor parameters.
counterfactuals.output:
An invention is provided for diagnosing failures of fuel-related sensors in an internal combustion engine by using two independent estimation approaches and comparing their results.

The system includes a first estimator that determines a fuel-related quantity, such as injected fuel amount, fuel pressure, air-fuel ratio, or sensor deviation, based on combustion information obtained from the engine. This combustion information may include cylinder pressure, heat release rate, combustion phasing, indicated torque, misfire information, exhaust characteristics, or other combustion-derived data. The first estimator performs estimation under a plurality of different engine operating conditions, such as different loads, speeds, injection timings, injection quantities, air amounts, or combustion modes, so that the effect of a sensor abnormality can be distinguished from normal engine variation.

A second estimator independently determines the same or corresponding fuel-related quantity using characteristic parameters of the relevant sensor. These parameters may include sensor output voltage, offset, gain, response delay, temperature characteristic, learned correction value, drift amount, linearity, or other known sensor behavior. The second estimator therefore evaluates the sensor based on its own signal characteristics rather than primarily on combustion results.

A diagnostic unit compares the estimation result from the first estimator with the estimation result from the second estimator. If the two estimates agree within an allowable range, the sensor is judged to be operating normally. If a deviation between the estimates exceeds a threshold, or if the deviation appears only under specific operating conditions, the diagnostic unit determines that a failure, deterioration, drift, sticking, response delay, or calibration error exists in one or more fuel-related sensors.

The invention may be applied to sensors such as fuel pressure sensors, fuel injection quantity sensors, oxygen sensors, air-fuel ratio sensors, fuel temperature sensors, or sensors used for controlling injection timing and fuel delivery. By combining combustion-based estimation under varying engine conditions with sensor-characteristic-based estimation, the system improves diagnostic accuracy and reduces false failure detection caused by transient engine operation or combustion disturbance.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Produce a concise patent abstract about a diagnostic apparatus that determines whether a combustion sensor or characteristic sensor has failed based on fuel molecular structure mixing ratio estimates.
counterfactuals.output: A diagnostic apparatus for an internal combustion engine estimates a mixing ratio of fuel molecular structures in supplied fuel based on outputs from a combustion sensor and a fuel characteristic sensor. The apparatus compares the respective molecular-structure mixing ratio estimates, or values derived therefrom, and determines a failure of at least one of the combustion sensor or the characteristic sensor when a deviation between the estimates exceeds a predetermined threshold.
